name: Autosomal Recessive Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple punctate hyperkeratotic papules on the palms and soles
Consistent autosomal recessive inheritance pattern in family history
Histological confirmation showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis
Exclusion of other forms of palmoplantar keratoderma by clinical and genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of punctate palmoplantar keratoderma lesions with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern and histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but causative gene(s) may not be identified in all cases.

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia with compact orthokeratosis
Negative fungal cultures in absence of secondary infection
genetic: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with autosomal recessive punctate palmoplantar keratoderma (e.g., AAGAB mutations)
Genetic testing confirming autosomal recessive inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic punctate keratoderma lesions
Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Linear hyperkeratotic lesions rather than punctate

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma lesions with ulceration
Signs of secondary infection with systemic symptoms
Family history suggestive of syndromic keratoderma or associated systemic disease
